correctness.rationale: The unqualified arbitrary sampled anchor in the frozen text cannot include geometry-dependent choices. For example, if the shortest gap goes clockwise from positions 1 to 2, then L_1=L_2 almost surely, whereas (1) gives Var(L_1-L_2)=2(pi^2/6-C)>0. The complete corrected RESULT.md and SLOGAN.txt in /workspace/repairs/1 impose a preassigned sampling label for the covariance and spectrum and distinguish the invariant sample average. Under the corrected scope, conditioning on the anchor makes the sorted relative offsets uniform order statistics; the gap law is Dirichlet(1,...,1). Independent rate-one exponentials divided by their gamma total realize this law; the normalized gaps are independent of that total. Each adjacent-gap minimum before normalization is rate two. Nonneighboring minima have disjoint inputs, and neighboring minima have joint survival exp(-u-v-max(u,v)); clipped indicator-log integrals pass to the limit in L^2 and give the stated positive shared covariance. Substituting v=xu on the half-plane v<=u and integrating in u gives 2 times the integral of [log(1+x)-log(1+x/2)]/x on [0,1], hence C. Normalizing subtracts precisely trigamma(n) from every matrix entry. Fourier diagonalization gives the spectrum including the triangle; the alternating-series bounds on Li_2(-1/2) and n trigamma(n)<=n/(n-1) verify strict positivity and the stated signs. The mean is -H_(n-1) and the average variance is the constant-mode eigenvalue divided by n. For the CLT, linearize log of the total at n, use H_(n-1)-gamma-log(n)=O(1/n), and remove one cyclic term from the stationary one-dependent sum. The covariance of log of the exponential minimum with the sum of its two inputs is one, since the sum equals twice the minimum plus an independent exponential excess. The resulting long-run variance is pi^2/6+2C-1. For n=2 both positions have 2 rho uniform on [0,1] and yield variance one. The frozen verification and script were inspected, not executed; neither Monte Carlo nor numerical quadrature is used as a universal proof.
